title.narrative: Accountability, cohesion and trust for non-discrimination, ownership and wellbeing

description.narrative: NPC works to raise awareness and build consensus on what is needed to achieve peace, healing, reconciliation and equality in Sri Lanka. This project follows on from previous programme phases implemented over a period of seven years so far, focusing on influential intermediaries and fostering discourse on the process of conflict transformation. The channel for delivering this work is the District Inter-Religious Committee (DIRC) which have been formed by NPC throughout the country. Members of the DIRCs – religious leaders, professionals, journalists, academics - are trusted leaders who take the message of peace and reconciliation to the wider community. The DIRCs also play a strong role in conflict mitigation and resolution at local level, and in heading off potential triggers of conflict (such as malicious rumours) before they can get properly under way. Over recent years the DIRCs have been strengthened and expanded into additional areas, and their impact increased by the creation of satellite committees. In the next phase of this work 2026-29 the DIRCs will be supported to continue their work of awareness raising, dialogue and conflict resolution.
